title: Embed a thin skin strip in paraffin: press it flat with forceps while the other hand slides the mould onto the cold spot
instruction: Embed the skin strip that lies in the paraffin-filled mould on the warm plate. With the warm forceps, move it to the middle of the mould and press it flat, inked face down. Keep it pressed with the forceps while the other hand slides the mould across onto the cold spot, and keep pressing until the wax at the bottom has set. Then put the forceps back in their well and move both hands away.
context: Laboratory research automation: paraffin embedding is the routine hand step between tissue processing and sectioning in histology labs, research and clinical, done at an embedding station with warm forceps. Thin specimens such as skin curl; the technician holds them flat against the bottom of the metal mould with forceps until the paraffin has cooled (US patent 8,329,120, which also notes how hard it is to lift the forceps away without dislodging the piece). A strip that sets curled is sectioned at an angle: its sections miss part of the cut face, or the block is re-melted and embedded again. The standard sequence (ARUP Laboratories, histology terms): lay the piece cut face down in the middle, press it flat, move the mould onto the cold spot and keep pressing until the bottom layer sets. One hand keeps the press while the other slides the mould, so the forceps must follow the moving mould.
setup: All positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left); heights above the table. A benchtop paraffin embedding station, fixed: grey housing 20 x 27 cm; its flat work surface 6 cm up is a warm aluminium plate (60 C) from y = 0.5 to 16.5 and x = 22 to 38, a 1 cm black insulating strip at y = -0.5 to 0.5, and a blue cold block (-5 C) from y = -7.5 to -0.5 and x = 24 to 36, all flush; a paraffin tank behind it (x 40 to 46). On the warm plate at (30, 6.5): a stainless steel base mould, 24 x 37 mm inside and 9 mm deep (its long side along y), holding 6 mm of molten paraffin and one processed skin strip (pig skin, 8 x 10 x 2 mm, its cut face, the face to be sectioned, inked black), dropped in 6 mm from the middle towards the far (+y) end, curled up at one end. Warm stainless embedding forceps, 150 mm, tips closed, stand tips-down in a heated 12 mm square well at (25, 14.5) on the warm plate. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Measured once the block has cooled and been knocked out of the mould: a photo of the block face against a millimetre scale, and the trial video. Score 0 if at any time a gripper or its sleeve touched the wax in the mould, the mould tipped more than 10 degrees or was lifted more than 1 cm, or the strip left the mould. Score 0 unless the mould stood with its whole floor on the cold spot for 8 s with the strip in it, and unless the strip set flat: in the face photo its black inked outline is sharp all round, with no stretch longer than 1 mm greyed under wax (a curled end lies under the face and shows grey). If flat: 0.5; plus 0.25 if the strip's centre is within 3 mm of the block face's centre (where its diagonals cross); plus 0.25 for the forceps back in their well and no gripper within 3 cm of the mould. Full score 1.0 when all hold, still for 1 s; the trial then ends. Doing nothing scores 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
reset_notes: Strips: one batch of 8 x 10 x 2 mm strips cut from processed pig skin, cut face inked, prepared once by any histology lab; each trial's strip is recovered by re-melting its block at 60 C and reused. Start: the strip is dropped in cut face down near the far end; before each trial its far end must stand 2 to 4 mm off the mould floor (read against the 9 mm wall); a strip that lies flatter is retired. Paraffin 56 to 58 C, 6 mm deep, poured from a 60 C wax bath. Station: an embedding station, or a lab hot plate under a 6 mm aluminium plate at 60 C beside an aluminium block on a fresh cold pack, flush, a 1 cm PTFE strip between; a thermometer on the block reads -5 to 0 C at the start. Grippers wear silicone sleeves; wax on a sleeve sets in seconds and is peeled off.
fidelity: Paraffin is not a fluid here. Declared rule: a strip the forceps' tips have not pressed for 0.3 s curls (held with one end 2 mm up, tilted 15 degrees); pressing it while the wax is molten lays it flat again; moved while curled it is left 4 mm behind; curled on the cold block, the curl sets. After 8 s on the cold block the strip is fixed where it lies. The strip is rigid, 2 g for the solver. The forceps are one rigid body, tips closed.
